Rather than seeking "the one," we benefit from synthesizing the best: Aristotle for virtues, Hume for skepticism, Nietzsche for vitality. Socially, it risks division; better to embrace fallibilism (Popper): all philosophies provisionally wrong, open to revision. A more accurate rephrasing: "Among all philosophies, elements from many are probably correct." 

This reflection reveals the statement as more rhetorical than robust, inviting deeper inquiry over dogmatic closure.
